slides.explanation: Millions of people were suddenly locked out of their own bank accounts. That is roughly the size of a mid-sized nation unable to access their savings.

slides.headline: Resignation did not stop the impeachment
slides.explanation: Peña announced he was stepping down on social media, but the lower house voted to impeach him just minutes later.
This report is verified by three independent outlets including France 24, NPR World, and BBC World. Their consensus confirms the timeline of this legislative action.

caption:
Paraguay is in political turmoil.

President Santiago Peña has resigned and was impeached by the lower house in the same hour.

The move follows widespread protests sparked by a banking crisis. Millions of citizens were left unable to access their money after a bank takeover.

Lawmakers voted unanimously to remove him from office immediately after his resignation announcement on social media. How do you think a country stabilizes after such a sudden leadership vacuum?

story.title: Paraguay's president Peña impeached moments after resigning over banking scandal
story.summary: Paraguay’s lower house voted unanimously to impeach President Santiago Peña on Thursday, just minutes after he announced his resignation on X. Protesters have rallied in the streets since the takeover of a bank linked to Peña blocked millions of people, including pensioners, from accessing their money.
